key_insight: Leading LLMs can generate diverse colonoscopy-prep dialogues, but correctness and safety vary enough that automated deferral safeguards may be needed.
clinical_relevance: Conversational AI could help patients understand bowel-prep instructions and ask questions, potentially reducing avoidable colonoscopy delays from poor preparation.
method: Generated 250 patient–AI Coach dialogues per model across 5 leading LLMs.
Used 3–7 question-answer pairs on diet, medications, and prep topics, with human expert review plus LLM-as-a-judge scoring.
Measured correctness, harmfulness, error types, and question diversity; compared models with permutation tests and inter-rater agreement checks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports multi-rater human evaluation, automatic judging, and diversity metrics across 1,250 total dialogues, with model differences tested at the dialogue level.
watch_item: Synthetic dialogue results may not translate directly to real patients, and any clinical deployment would need careful oversight, escalation pathways, and validation against harmful or misleading advice.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
